messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@maplehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: MSA/Order Form redlines (SLA language)

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's latency profile. Procurement is starting the contract run and we’ve attached a set of proposed redlines specifically around SLA and support: uptime measurement, maintenance windows, service credit caps and response times.

High level asks from Maple Health:
- Uptime target: 99.95% (monthly)
- P1 response: 30 minutes; P1 restore target: 4 hours
- Service credits: uncapped tiered credits (no hard cap requested)
- No scheduled maintenance windows during our core hours (Mon–Fri 08:00–20:00 ET)

I’ve attached MapleHealth_SLA_Redlines_v1.docx. Can you confirm who at Redwood will lead the redline review and a rough timeline for legal + ops signoff? We’d like to get an initial position this week so our internal counsel can prioritize.

Best,
Elena
Elena Martinez
Sr. Procurement Manager | Maple Health

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.inference.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@maplehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: MSA/Order Form redlines (SLA language)

Elena — thanks for the redlines and clear asks. Looping in Marissa (Ops/Customer Success) and Karthik (Legal) for technical and contract comments. Quick triage from our side:

- Uptime: 99.95% is above our standard hosted-tier guarantee. We can propose a commercial uplift + dedicated capacity (Reserved) to meet 99.95; for hosted we typically provide 99.9%. We’ll outline options (hosted vs. dedicated) and corresponding credit calculations.
- Response times: P1 30m SLA excursions are operationally tight for multi-tenant hosted endpoints unless we agree on dedicated capacity and a higher support tier. For hosted we can commit to P1 1 hour (initial response) with a 4-hour operational triage target; for Dedicated we can target 30m response with a defined on-call rotation.
- Service credits: we typically cap monthly credits at a percentage of monthly fees (commonly 100% cap over a rolling 12-month window). We can propose a middle ground: tiered credits up to 200% of monthly recurring charges for the first year with a review clause.
- Maintenance windows: we do schedule rolling patch windows but can agree to a blackout during your defined core hours for Dedicated capacity or offer scheduled maintenance with 72-hour notice and make-good credits if unscheduled impact occurs.

I attached a short summary (RWI_SLA_Response_Summary_20260301.pdf) with our suggested starting positions. Karthik — can you confirm any absolute legal no-go items (e.g., uncapped credits, make-whole obligations, third-party infra guarantees)? Marissa — can you confirm ops impact and whether a Dedicated commitment would be required to meet their uptime/response asks?

We’re available for a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Attachments: RWI_SLA_Response_Summary_20260301.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.inference.com>, Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@maplehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T15:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: MSA/Order Form redlines (SLA language)

Priya / Elena — quick legal read and redline guidance: 

1) Uncapped credits: Redwood’s standard position is to cap service credits to a percentage of Monthly Recurring Charges (MRC); unlimited or uncapped credits expose us to disproportionate risk. We can offer a temporary higher cap for the first 12 months tied to committed spend, then revert to standard caps.

2) Measurement & exclusions: we need clear metric definitions (how uptime is measured — region-by-region, rolling windows, excluded causes such as customer misconfiguration, third-party infra outages). Please add precise definitions in the SLA appendix so we can avoid disputes.

3) P1 response/restore: legal is ok to propose tighter response times if ops confirms capacity guarantees (e.g., Dedicated nodes + on-call). Otherwise we need to add a clause limiting response obligations for multi-tenant hosted services.

4) Maintenance blackout: we can agree to blackout windows in the Order Form for core hours, but need to include emergency maint carveouts and notice periods (48–72 hours for scheduled).

5) Indemnity/Service-level interplay: any credits must be the exclusive remedy for SLA breaches; we’ll resist language that permits termination or additional indemnity solely for uptime misses.

Action items: 
- Priya / Marissa: provide an ops confirmation (dedicated vs hosted) and proposed credit cap schedule.
- Elena: if Maple is willing to consider a committed capacity option (12–24 months), k please indicate an expected MRC range so we can calibrate the credit cap.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Thanks — helpful framing. We’re open to a committed capacity approach if the numbers make sense. High-level responses from Maple Health:

- Committed capacity: we can consider a 12–18 month committed plan (target MRC: USD 75k–120k / month) depending on uplift. That should be sufficient to justify a higher uptime guarantee.
- Service credits: we can accept a capped model if the cap scales with committed spend (e.g., 150% MRC cap at $75k MRC, 200% at $100k+).
- Response times: willing to accept a Dedicated route for the 30-minute P1 response if Redwood provides documented on-call commitment and escalation contact details.
- Maintenance: we need the blackout for core hours in the Order Form for the first 18 months; emergency patch carveouts are acceptable with post-event reporting and a one-time credit if it materially impacted production.

Next steps:
1) Can Redwood share a draft Order Form appendix with the committed-capacity pricing tiers + proposed credit table?
2) Let’s schedule a 30m call tomorrow (2026-03-05) 10:00–10:30 ET to align on the draft and confirm the DocuSign/Redlines path.

If you send the appendix today we’ll circulate it to our GC before the call.

Regards,
Elena
Elena Martinez
Sr. Procurement Manager | Maple Health
